thread:
chloe: quick q — mapping API errors to SDK exceptions. writing a short guidance page. what should py/ts users expect for 400/401/403/429/5xx?
ben: short checklist: 400 -> BadRequestError, 401 -> AuthError, 403 -> PermissionError, 429 -> RateLimitError (retryable), 5xx -> ServerError (non-idempotent ops should not auto-retry). also include RequestId on all these for debugging.
chloe: perfect. do we include the raw http code on the exception object? customers asked for that.
alice: yes — exceptions expose .status_code, .code (internal api error code string), .request_id. TS/JS uses `status`, `error_code`, `requestId`.
chloe: example mapping for python?
ben: paste quick snippet — catch + rethrow pattern we recommend:
```python
# recommended pattern in docs
from redwood_sdk import client, exceptions

try:
    resp = client.generate(prompt)
except exceptions.RateLimitError as e:
    # e.request_id is set
    logger.warning(f"rate limited, req={e.request_id}, retry-after={e.headers.get('Retry-After')}")
    raise
except exceptions.AuthError as e:
    logger.error(f"auth failed req={e.request_id} code={e.status_code}")
    raise
except exceptions.APIError as e:
    # fallback for unexpected server errors
    logger.exception(f"api error req={e.request_id} status={e.status_code}")
    raise
```
chloe: nice. how about streaming? we've seen users confused when a stream dies mid-message — what's the canonical exception and how to resume?
alice: streaming errors: StreamDisconnect (server closed/timeout), StreamInterrupted (client aborted), StreamProtocolError (parse errors). For StreamDisconnect we include `resume_token` when available so clients can request only the missing range. Not all models support resume.
sam: ops point — make sure our HTTP/gateway logs always include `request_id` header (ri_*) and correlate with infra traces. sample log: 
[INFO] 2026-02-12T14:23:12.345Z service=gateway req=ri_9f3a1b POST /v1/generate 429 "Too Many Requests" latency=123ms

infra-bot: deployed logpath change to include req id in 3 services (:white_check_mark:)
chloe: do we standardize `request_id` format? i've seen ri_ and r_ prefixes.
ben: agreed to standardize on `ri_<hex>` in spec. we'll accept legacy `r_` but convert in SDK to `request_id` field. docs should recommend logging `req={request_id}`.
chloe: what about retry semantics? guide wants to recommend exponential backoff + jitter for 429, and idempotency keys for POSTs.
alice: yes. small note: streaming retry for partial content — only safe if model/container supports resume_token + deterministic outputs; otherwise re-run with same prompt but include `initial_sequence` to dedupe on client side. add a warning.
chloe: i'll add an example for JS showing `fetch` + reconnect with `resumeToken`.
ben: also surface HTTP headers on exceptions: `X-Request-ID`, `Retry-After`, `X-Model-Variant`. makes debugging easier.
sam: ping @chloe — can you add a sample logger snippet showing `structured` logging? ops team will copy it.
chloe: will do. draft snippet for structured logs: 
```python
log = {
  "ts": now_iso(),
  "level": "warn",
  "msg": "request throttled",
  "request_id": e.request_id,
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "status": e.status_code
}
logger.warn(json.dumps(log))
```
ben: :thumbsup: Also add a tiny troubleshooting FAQ row: "If you see StreamDisconnect + no request_id, check gateway sidecar version < 1.8.0".
chloe: good call. last q — who owns adding `request_id` to all sdk exception constructors? is that infra or client-lib?
alice: SDKs should populate it from response headers. infra ensures headers exist end-to-end. sam is owning infra rollout for header stabilization.
sam: yep, infra will finish header rollout by EOD Friday and post here when done.
chloe: great — i'll update devex doc and ping for review. tagging @ben @alice for quick review when done. :eyes:
ben: i can review tomorrow morning.
alice: will do after standup.
chloe: thanks all — closing this thread after doc PR. :white_check_mark:
